nodes.text: Define $\epsilon_n$ to be maximal such that there exists some choice of congruence class $a_p$ for all primes $n^{\epsilon_n}<p\leq n$ such that every integer in $[1,n]$ satisfies at least one of the congruences $\equiv a_p\pmod{p}$. Estimate $\epsilon_n$ - in particular is it true that $\epsilon_n=o(1)$?

#688 : [Er79d] [Er80,p.106] number theory Erdős could prove\[\epsilon_n \gg \frac{\log\log\log n}{\log\log n}.\]See also [687] , [689] , and [1200] .
